evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted check only compares manager PID and invocation ID. The same snapshot structure carries a boot_id (the reboot comparison at lines 1117-1123 reads `boot_id_before`/`boot_id_after` from snapshot objects), so a guest reboot between the restart and the manager after-inspect can produce a different manager PID and invocation ID and falsely satisfy manager_restarted even though the observations span different boots. That is an existing correctness gap in the intended isolated-manager-restart evidence, not a new requirement. Requiring both manager snapshots to have nonempty equal `boot_id` values while retaining the PID/invocation checks is the minimal compatible fix.
